sections.title: Primary data
sections.description: These records supplied the sequences, annotations, and measured values used by this release. A download marked ‘project-derived’ is a processed table, not an unmodified publisher file. The full genome inputs fetched during the build are not committed to this repository.

items.citation: Yu J, Liberton M, Cliften PF, Head RD, Jacobs JM, Smith RD, Koppenaal DW, Brand JJ, Pakrasi HB. Synechococcus elongatus UTEX 2973, a fast growing cyanobacterial chassis for biosynthesis using light and CO₂. Scientific Reports 5, 8132 (2015). doi:10.1038/srep08132.
items.contribution: Original sequencing and characterization of UTEX 2973, the genome later obtained here through NCBI RefSeq. The site uses the current NCBI annotation of that assembly; it does not import this paper’s proteomics measurements or infer growth effects from its results.

items.citation: NCBI RefSeq. Synechococcus elongatus UTEX 2973 assembly GCF_000817325.1 (ASM81732v1); annotation release RS_2026_05_13.
items.contribution: Source of the UTEX 2973 genome, coding sequences, locus tags, gene products, tRNA annotations, coordinates, and release checks. The site derives its gene features and genomic tRNA-copy table from this pinned assembly and annotation; tRNA gene copies are not measured tRNA abundance or charging. NCBI does not state a dataset-specific redistribution license for these retained files; NCBI data-use policies apply.

items.citation: Tan X, Hou S, Song K, Georg J, Klähn S, Lu X, Hess WR. The primary transcriptome of the fast-growing cyanobacterium Synechococcus elongatus UTEX 2973. Biotechnology for Biofuels 11, 218 (2018). doi:10.1186/s13068-018-1215-8.
items.contribution: Primary UTEX 2973 dRNA-seq source for mapped transcription-start sites, per-site counts, and the authors’ condition-versus-control DESeq2 results. Table S1 supplies two biological culture replicates per condition (control, dark, high light, high temperature). The site also computes a separately labelled, pooled TSS-initiation score. These are initiation measurements, not replicated gene-body transcript abundance. Publisher processed data: Figshare 5712016 (CC BY 4.0). Both repository TSVs are project-derived extracts, not the original XLSX supplement.

items.citation: Simkovsky R et al. Transcriptomic and Phenomic Investigations Reveal Elements in Biofilm Repression and Formation in the Cyanobacterium Synechococcus elongatus PCC 7942. Frontiers in Microbiology 13, 899150 (2022). doi:10.3389/fmicb.2022.899150; GEO GSE205444.
items.contribution: The optional RNA-abundance overlay averages the three wild-type, fresh-BG-11, day-one DESeq2-normalized count samples from GSE205444, then maps unambiguous shared protein IDs to UTEX 2973. The measured organism is PCC 7942, not UTEX 2973. The repository TSV is a project-derived mapped table; no dataset-specific GEO redistribution license was located.

items.citation: Adomako M et al. Comparative Genomics of Synechococcus elongatus Explains the Phenotypic Diversity of the Strains. mBio 13, e00862-22 (2022). doi:10.1128/mbio.00862-22; Data Set S1. PCC 7942 essentiality calls in this workbook derive from Rubin BE et al., Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences 112, E6634–E6643 (2015), doi:10.1073/pnas.1519220112.
items.contribution: Data Set S1 provides PCC 7942 essentiality calls, explicit PCC and UTEX 2973 current locus IDs, and pangenome rows. The site joins only matching, unique PCC RefSeq protein cross-references to current UTEX CDSs. The calls remain PCC 7942 measurements under Rubin's assay conditions; applying them to a UTEX candidate is a labelled assumption, not native essentiality. The article's Data Set S1 legend specifies CC BY 4.0; the workbook does not repeat the notice.

downloads.kind: Original Adomako Data Set S1 workbook, CC BY 4.0

items.citation: NCBI RefSeq. Synechococcus elongatus PCC 7942 assembly GCF_000012525.1 (ASM1252v1).
items.contribution: The pinned PCC 7942 GFF provides historical and current PCC locus tags and RefSeq protein accessions for the exact, ambiguity-preserving cross-strain mapping of GSE205444 values. It does not make the PCC expression data a UTEX measurement. NCBI data-use policies apply; no dataset-specific license was stated.

items.citation: Gene Ontology Consortium. NCBI-hosted UTEX 2973 GO association file (GO version 2026-03-25); Ashburner M et al., Nature Genetics 25, 25–29 (2000), doi:10.1038/75556; Gene Ontology Consortium, The Gene Ontology knowledgebase in 2026, Nucleic Acids Research (2025), doi:10.1093/nar/gkaf1292.
items.contribution: Evidence-coded Gene Ontology associations in gene details come from the NCBI-generated GAF, joined to this release’s UTEX loci; the derived table marks ambiguous protein-to-locus expansions. GO data and products: © 1999–2026 Gene Ontology Consortium, CC BY 4.0, provided AS-IS without warranty. The linked policy requests both cited GO papers and release identification; no GO enrichment analysis is claimed.

sections.title: Methods, design, validation & software
sections.description: These works guided calculations, interpretation, validation, software implementation, or explicit source-admission decisions. Their experimental measurements were not imported as gene-level data unless listed above.

items.citation: Ungerer J, Wendt KE, Hendry JI, Maranas CD, Pakrasi HB. Comparative genomics reveals the molecular determinants of rapid growth of the cyanobacterium Synechococcus elongatus UTEX 2973. Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences 115, E11761–E11770 (2018). doi:10.1073/pnas.1814912115.
items.contribution: Reviewed as a possible native UTEX 2973 gene-body transcriptomics and allele/phenotype source. Its supplemental wild-type TPM survey lacks biological replicates, so no expression values or growth-effect labels from this paper are integrated in the current site.

items.citation: Hassanien A et al. Gene expression analysis reveals genes related to heavy metals and produced water exposure in Synechococcus elongatus. International Microbiology 28, 2697–2708 (2025). doi:10.1007/s10123-025-00715-x.
items.contribution: Assessed as another UTEX 2973 transcriptomics candidate. The accessible supplement provides selected genes, not a validated genome-wide, per-replicate baseline abundance matrix; no values from it are integrated.

items.citation: Rubin BE et al. The essential gene set of a photosynthetic organism. Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences 112, E6634–E6643 (2015). doi:10.1073/pnas.1519220112.
items.contribution: Original PCC 7942 transposon-screen evidence behind the calls republished in Adomako 2022 Data Set S1. The assay used BG-11 at 30 C with multiple light and culture regimes. The original Rubin Dataset S3 is not redistributed here. Its calls are shown as PCC observations and an explicit cross-strain assumption for UTEX candidates; they do not establish UTEX essentiality or recoding outcomes.

items.citation: Ungerer J, Lin PC, Chen HY, Pakrasi HB. Adjustments to Photosystem Stoichiometry and Electron Transfer Proteins Are Key to the Remarkably Fast Growth of the Cyanobacterium Synechococcus elongatus UTEX 2973. mBio 9, e02327-17 (2018). doi:10.1128/mBio.02327-17.
items.contribution: Reports similar growth rates at a PCC-7942-compatible 400 micromol photons m^-2 s^-1 light intensity, while documenting substantially different growth optima. This condition-specific observation motivates review of, but does not validate, transferring PCC gene-essentiality calls to UTEX 2973.

items.citation: Sharp PM, Li WH. The codon adaptation index—a measure of directional synonymous codon usage bias, and its potential applications. Nucleic Acids Research 15, 1281–1295 (1987). doi:10.1093/nar/15.3.1281.
items.contribution: Defines the CAI method used for genome-derived codon-adaptation values. This project chooses its own release-pinned 71-gene reference set; that set is a convention, not expression data from the paper.

items.citation: dos Reis M, Savva R, Wernisch L. Solving the riddle of codon usage preferences: a test for translational selection. Nucleic Acids Research 32, 5036–5044 (2004). doi:10.1093/nar/gkh834.
items.contribution: Source of the tRNA adaptation index convention, selective wobble constraints, and zero-weight substitution. The anticodon copy counts used here come from this UTEX annotation, not the paper’s organisms; tAI is a proxy, not measured expression.

items.citation: Soma A et al. An RNA-modifying enzyme that governs both the codon and amino acid specificities of isoleucine tRNA. Molecular Cell 12, 689–698 (2003). doi:10.1016/S1097-2765(03)00346-0.
items.contribution: Supports the bacterial lysidine/TilS convention used to model the annotated Ile-CAT tRNA as decoding ATA rather than ATG. This is a biochemical rule from other bacteria, not direct measurement of UTEX 2973 tRNA modification or charging.

items.citation: Wright F. The ‘effective number of codons’ used in a gene. Gene 87, 23–29 (1990). doi:10.1016/0378-1119(90)90491-9.
items.contribution: Defines the ENC synonymous-codon-bias metric and its GC3-based expected curve used by the site. Short-family substitutions and the difference-from-expectation are labelled as implementation conventions.

items.citation: Coleman JR et al. Virus attenuation by genome-scale changes in codon pair bias. Science 320, 1784–1787 (2008). doi:10.1126/science.1155761.
items.contribution: Motivates the codon-pair-bias / log-odds feature. This site estimates its own amino-acid-pair-conditioned scores from the UTEX genome; it does not import the paper’s viral measurements or infer attenuation outcomes.

items.citation: Love MI, Huber W, Anders S. Moderated estimation of fold change and dispersion for RNA-seq data with DESeq2. Genome Biology 15, 550 (2014). doi:10.1186/s13059-014-0550-8.
items.contribution: Explains the DESeq2-normalized counts and reported differential-transcription statistics supplied by the two source studies. This site does not rerun DESeq2 or call gene-level differential expression from Tan’s TSS rows.

items.citation: McInnes L, Healy J, Saul N, Großberger L. UMAP: Uniform Manifold Approximation and Projection. Journal of Open Source Software 3, 861 (2018). doi:10.21105/joss.00861; umap-learn software.
items.contribution: The build pipeline uses umap-learn to place genes in the recoding-risk projection. Coordinates are a visualization of computed UTEX features, not evidence that nearby genes share biological function.

items.citation: Pedregosa F et al. Scikit-learn: Machine Learning in Python. Journal of Machine Learning Research 12, 2825–2830 (2011).
items.contribution: The build pipeline uses StandardScaler and PCA for codon-usage coordinates and projection inputs. The in-browser two-axis projection also uses project code, not a copied scikit-learn model.

items.citation: Lorenz R et al. ViennaRNA Package 2.0. Algorithms for Molecular Biology 6, 26 (2011). doi:10.1186/1748-7188-6-26; ViennaRNA 2.7.2.
items.contribution: ViennaRNA computes local minimum-free-energy folds for selected wild-type and recoded RNA windows. The browser ships a locally compiled 2.7.2 engine; the project-specific wrapper does not change the algorithms or parameter tables. Credit to the ViennaRNA authors and the Institute for Theoretical Chemistry, University of Vienna. Its custom redistribution license and build record are retained at site/vendor/viennarna/PROVENANCE.md.

items.citation: Emscripten 4.0.15 and bundled runtime components: musl, LLVM compiler-rt, Joseph A. Adams’s JSON library, and Doug Lea’s dlmalloc; upstream licenses retained with the ViennaRNA browser build.
items.contribution: Emscripten compiled the ViennaRNA engine to WebAssembly and supplied its JavaScript/runtime glue. The component-specific notices and licenses are retained under site/vendor/viennarna/; this is software attribution, not a source of biological data.

items.citation: Cock PJA et al. Biopython: freely available Python tools for computational molecular biology and bioinformatics. Bioinformatics 25, 1422–1423 (2009). doi:10.1093/bioinformatics/btp163.
items.contribution: The data-build and consistency checks use Biopython to parse biological sequence records, translate CDSs, and apply codon tables. No Biopython code is bundled with the site.

items.citation: NCBI. The Genetic Codes: The Bacterial, Archaeal and Plant Plastid Code (translation table 11).
items.contribution: Defines the bacterial codon-to-amino-acid and alternative initiation assignments used to interpret UTEX coding sequences and validate synonymous recoding; the initiation position is handled separately from ordinary codons.

items.citation: Harris CR et al. Array programming with NumPy. Nature 585, 357–362 (2020). doi:10.1038/s41586-020-2649-2.
items.contribution: NumPy arrays support the feature build and independent consistency checks; this package provides computation, not external gene measurements.

items.citation: Virtanen P et al. SciPy 1.0: fundamental algorithms for scientific computing in Python. Nature Methods 17, 261–272 (2020). doi:10.1038/s41592-019-0686-2.
items.contribution: SciPy supports statistical integration checks and is a declared build-environment dependency; it contributes no biological measurements to the site.

items.citation: openpyxl, Python library for reading and writing Excel workbooks (project documentation).
items.contribution: Used to extract the published Tan 2018 Table S1 XLSX into the checked TSV without treating workbook formatting or recalculation as biological data.

items.citation: McKinney W. Data Structures for Statistical Computing in Python. Proceedings of the 9th Python in Science Conference, 51–56 (2010); pandas library.
items.contribution: pandas is a declared Python scientific-stack dependency in the build environment. The current core build does not directly import pandas or take biological observations from it; it remains credited as part of the declared software environment.

items.citation: pytest development team. pytest: Python testing framework (project documentation).
items.contribution: Runs the Python feature, integration, provenance, and source-ledger tests. It is a validation tool and supplies no biological data or browser runtime code.

items.citation: TypeSafe, System One / Jev model (jev-1.13.0); project CAI reference-set semantic audit, 2026-09-19.
items.contribution: Used only to independently classify RefSeq product names for validation of the 71-gene CAI reference-set rule. Disagreements were reviewed; the model did not automatically change published membership or supply biological ground truth.

items.citation: Wang W, Liu X, Peng Z, Yang J. The trRosettaRNA server for RNA structure prediction. Nature Protocols 21 (2026). doi:10.1038/s41596-026-01356-8.
items.contribution: External form opened by the hand-off. This site prepares files but does not submit sequences or capture returned models.

items.citation: Wang W, Feng C, Han R, Wang Z, Ye L, Du Z, Wei H, Zhang F, Peng Z, Yang J. trRosettaRNA: automated prediction of RNA 3D structure with transformer network. Nature Communications 14, 7266 (2023). doi:10.1038/s41467-023-42528-4.
items.contribution: Method paper for trRosettaRNA. The official standalone package documents A3M and custom dot-bracket/CT inputs; its Apache-2.0 code and the separate PyRosetta licence remain external terms.
